purpose: Track exact, non-overlapping read ranges for oversized audit units. Entries in this ledger remain outside COMPLETE coverage until every source line and required history/test evidence has been reviewed.

notes: Imports show a very broad orchestration boundary spanning applications, connections, OAuth, secrets, catalogs, profiles, policy decisions, runtime slots, invocations, action requests, events, metrics, and runtime supervision.
OAuth registration uses an in-process single-flight map; later ranges must verify whether database leases and multi-instance recovery fully cover this lifecycle.
The generic service embeds Google Sheets-specific schemas, environment normalization, and catalog fallback behavior, indicating provider logic may not be isolated behind a connector boundary.
OAuth actor binding checks actor type, actor id, and optionally session id; missing persisted actor identity fails closed.

Class-3 static lease credentials require an explicit allowlist key and config path and return structured error details, while several other boundary failures in this range expose only English message text.

The range is dominated by schemas, conversion projections, and lifecycle helpers; no final correctness, security, reuse, or ownership decision is valid until the remaining ranges and tests are reviewed.

Tool-profile summaries and new-tool review projections are implemented in-memory over full profile, catalog, binding, and agent arrays; later callers must be checked for pagination and tenant-size bounds.

Risk classification combines annotations, explicit Notion tool lists, and verb heuristics, but an unrecognized or renamed mutation defaults to read, creating a fail-open classification risk unless catalog quarantine or review always intercepts it.

Remote MCP and OAuth helpers validate every manual redirect against the public-endpoint guard in authenticated public deployments, and local stdio enablement requires a trusted runtime host in that deployment profile.
The connection-token broker rate limit counts successful issuances and then proceeds without an atomic reservation, so concurrent mints can exceed the configured hourly limit.

Broker authorization requires an exact, condition-free connection_token.mint include in the narrowest active profiles; exclusions are evaluated only within each profile, so cross-profile include/exclude semantics require test confirmation.
The broker derives responsibleUserId from the run context snapshot; this range does not revalidate that accountable human against current organization membership or responsibility contracts.

Generic and Pages token exchange send a vault-resolved parent token to a configured exchange URL using direct fetch rather than the guarded remote fetch helper; configuration authority and later validation must be traced because this can become a credential-egress boundary.

The RFC 8693 branch labels a base64url-encoded JSON actor_token as a JWT without signing it, and the response path shown here does not re-check returned scope or cap an explicit upstream expiresAt to the requested TTL.
These are preliminary findings from this range only; final severity and reuse judgment remain invalid until invocation paths, mutations, tests, migrations, and the rest of the file are reviewed.

Runtime health loads every company slot and connection plus an hour of audit and call events, then aggregates in memory on each request; no query limit, pagination, pre-aggregation, or retention bound is visible in this range.
Operator stop/restart completes before the activity log write, so a logging failure can return an error after the runtime mutation already succeeded and make retries ambiguous.

Google Sheets ownership enforcement scans every non-archived connection across all companies and returns conflicting spreadsheet ids, coupling a provider-specific global uniqueness rule and cross-tenant scan to the generic service.

Default app-profile creation, default workspace-grant creation, and runtime-slot creation use select-then-insert flows without a transaction or conflict recovery in this range; concurrent callers depend on unseen database constraints and may surface errors.
Profile detail and new-tool review projections load full company catalogs and related entity sets, confirming the earlier scalability concern for large tenants.

New-tool review lists pending state, inserts allow entries, marks catalog rows reviewed, and advances the profile watermark through separate writes without a transaction or compare-and-set; partial failure and tools first seen during the review window can produce inconsistent or skipped review state.

Profile entry replacement deletes all entries before re-insertion, and secret-binding synchronization deletes all bindings before re-insertion, without a transaction in the shown code; validation reduces input errors but not database or process-failure gaps.

Remote MCP discovery validates only the initial endpoint and then uses fetch with default redirect following instead of the manual redirect-validation helper; redirect targets, request timeout, response-size limits, and parsing-depth limits are not enforced in this range.
Health status is persisted before its audit event, so audit failure can leave a successful state mutation paired with a failed request and incomplete traceability.
These remain range-local findings; database uniqueness constraints, route authorization, tests, and later transactional wrappers must be checked before assigning final severity or reuse status.

Catalog refresh performs one update or insert per discovered descriptor and then separate connection, runtime-slot, and audit writes without a surrounding transaction; large catalogs incur sequential N+1 writes and partial refresh states are possible.

New or changed tools are quarantined only when connection configuration enables it, and safeDefault exempts entries classified as read; combined with the earlier fail-open heuristic, an unknown mutation can become active without review.
No removal or disablement of catalog entries missing from the latest discovery response is visible in this range, so stale upstream capabilities may remain represented unless later code handles them.

The apps-needing-attention projection loads every company invocation solely to map pending action requests back to connections, plus complete profiles, entries, and active catalog sets, creating an avoidable tenant-growth cost.

The health sweep loads every active enabled connection across all companies before filtering staleness and slicing the requested limit in memory; it lacks a database limit, lease, or visible multi-worker claim in this range.

Example installation mutates application, connection, credential bindings, runtime slot, profile, entries, and company binding through separate upserts and delete-then-insert operations without an encompassing transaction.

The example smoke actor selects the first real company agent when one exists and writes policy-decision audit events under that agent identity, which conflicts with Company OS responsibility integrity because a fixture check can be attributed to a human-managed production principal that did not act.

Credential-scope type and id may be taken directly from connection OAuth configuration without validation in this range; later secret-access enforcement must be checked to determine whether this is merely metadata or an authority boundary.

OAuth metadata retrieval validates each followed URL through the guarded fetch helper, including advertised authorization-server metadata, which is a reusable defense pattern; actual authorization and token POST paths still require separate verification.
All observations remain provisional until the rest of the OAuth lifecycle, route authorization, schema constraints, and tests are fully reviewed.

OAuth metadata and token POSTs use the guarded remote-fetch helper, which rejects redirects for non-GET/HEAD requests; this is a reusable credential-egress defense, although response timeout and size limits remain absent in the shown path.

Dynamic client registration validates PKCE S256 and public-client compatibility plus strict client-id, secret-length, redirect-uri, grant-type, response-type, auth-method, and timestamp response fields.
DCR serialization is only an in-process single-flight with a database re-read; multiple service instances can still register separate clients concurrently before either persists its result.
DCR secret creation or rotation, connection update, and secret-binding synchronization are separate operations, so persistence failure can leave rotated or orphaned secrets and mismatched bindings.

The refresh lease uses a database JSON compare-and-set and refuses to take over an expired lease, favoring uncertainty safety over availability; it mixes injected now() with Date.now(), which complicates deterministic testing and clock control.

Critical preliminary concurrency risk: refresh rotates the existing refresh-token and access-token secrets before the guarded connection-row update. Because references use the latest version, a refresh that later loses the lease CAS can still change the effective credential observed by the winning connection state.

Refresh-token rotation and access-token rotation are also separate writes, so a crash between them can leave only part of the new OAuth credential set effective despite the later connection update never occurring.
The refresh response accepts provider scope and token type as metadata without visible enforcement against configured requested scopes in this range.

Gallery connection setup creates secrets and then mutates application, connection, bindings, and runtime state through a manual compensation path that continues beyond this range and must be reviewed before judging atomicity.
Final findings require the remaining setup rollback, callback lifecycle, secret service semantics, schema constraints, and concurrency tests.

Gallery-connect failure uses best-effort manual compensation for connection, application, and newly created secrets; runtime slots and bindings depend on cascade or separate behavior not shown, and rollback failures are swallowed.

Finishing a gallery connection correctly groups profile replacement, bindings, catalog review state, ask-first policies, connection activation, and application activation in one database transaction, a materially stronger reusable pattern than earlier flows.

Reconnect rotates existing secrets or creates new ones before connection update and health verification, with no rollback in this function; an invalid replacement can immediately supersede the last working latest-version credential and new secrets can survive later failure.
OAuth start accepts requested scopes without checking they are a subset of advertised or configured scopes in this range.

The generic OAuth start function accepts agent-requested subject and issue identifiers without validating their responsibility relationship in this range; the exported agent-specific wrapper and route-level authority must be traced before judging the boundary.
The OAuth interaction stores actor sessionId as sourceRunId, conflating session identity and run identity unless the caller guarantees they are identical.

Callback state is deleted before token exchange, secret persistence, grant/application updates, health check, and catalog refresh; transient downstream failure consumes the one-time state and forces a complete restart.

User-specific callback completion rotates or creates secrets, upserts the user grant, and resolves the issue interaction through separate writes without a transaction, allowing partial success and responsibility-record disagreement.
No dedicated OAuth start or completion audit event is visible in this range, despite credentials, user consent, and delegated authority changing materially.

Admin-defined local stdio templates accept arbitrary command, args, env keys, and tool descriptors; final safety depends on route authority, deployment restrictions, supervisor sandboxing, and schema constraints outside this range.

The exported agent-specific authorization wrapper validates an active run and exact responsibleUserId snapshot before delegating to generic OAuth start, narrowing the prior concern; it still does not revalidate current organization membership or a versioned responsibility contract here.
Smoke execution confirms that a fixture policy check can select the first real company agent and persist allow/deny audit records under that principal, creating false responsibility evidence.

Application ownerUserId is persisted without a same-company membership check in this service, while ownerAgentId is checked; plugin ownership is checked only for existence and requires global/plugin tenancy review.

Connection creation can create an application and then fail during secret validation, connection insert, default grant, binding sync, or runtime-slot creation without a transaction or compensation, leaving partial control-plane state.

Adding a default workspace grant clears existing defaults and inserts the replacement in separate writes, so failure or concurrency can leave zero or multiple defaults unless database constraints close the gap.

putConnectionInstalls removes installation rows but only adds profile bindings for requested installs; it does not delete access-extension bindings for removed installs, so uninstalling a connection can leave effective tool access behind.
Access-extension activity logs are written after the install transaction; logging failure can report an error after authority has already changed.

Connection update persists credential references before non-transactional binding synchronization and runtime-slot setup, while archive does not visibly revoke grants, remove profile bindings, quarantine catalog entries, or stop runtime slots in this range.

Pending action-request and profile listing endpoints are unpaginated and load complete tenant sets; invalid signed requests are cancelled as a side effect of listing without a dedicated audit event shown here.

Profile create, update with delete-then-insert entries, duplicate, and delete-with-reassignment span multiple writes without transactions, allowing partial profiles, lost entries, or duplicated assignments after failure.
Profile assignment reassignment is performed before profile deletion without a transaction; delete failure can leave both source and target assignments active.
Effective access unions allows across active profiles and applies excludes only inside each profile, confirming that one profile cannot centrally deny a capability granted by another peer profile.
User and workspace grant selection uses limit(1) without deterministic ordering when grantId is omitted, so multiple active grants can yield unstable credential choice.

The token broker properly requires an active run, active grant and connection, healthy credential state, explicit mint profile grant, policy approval, parent-scope subset, and refuses direct static/OAuth bearer projection.

Critical preliminary TTL issue: an exchange response with a far-future explicit expiresAt is returned unchanged; only the separately reported ttlSeconds value is clamped to 900, so the actual delivered token lifetime can exceed the promised ceiling.

Critical preliminary side-effect issue: after the upstream token is minted, issuance success, grant last-used, and two audit sinks are separate writes. A later failure enters the catch path, records failure, and returns an error even though a live token and possibly a success record already exist, making retries mint duplicates.
The returned minted scope is not revalidated as a subset of requested or parent scope before delivery and recording.
Run-decision projection maps action requests by invocation id to one row, silently discarding additional requests for the same invocation if the schema permits them.

MCP JSON preview keeps imported stdio commands draft-only and converts remote headers into credential-field declarations, but input/object-size limits and later secret conversion require route-level review.

The implementation source is now fully read; all severity, test adequacy, database-constraint, route-authority, and reuse conclusions remain provisional pending the 6996-line service test and linked schemas/routes/history.

notes: The suite uses real embedded Postgres plus Express route integration, providing stronger persistence and HTTP-contract evidence than isolated mocks.

Broker tests cover active-run enforcement, exact responsible-user subject matching, revoked grants, explicit mint permission, parent-scope denial, static credential refusal, OAuth bearer non-projection, secret-access evidence, and hash-only token persistence.

The successful exchange test asserts ttlSeconds is at most 900 but does not assert the returned expiresAt is bounded by 900 seconds, so it does not catch the implementation's far-future explicit-expiry defect.
The hourly rate-limit test is strictly sequential and provides no evidence for concurrent reservation safety.
Scoped-credential tests correctly fail closed when the requested scope cannot select the configured parent credential and verify no secret access occurs on denial.
Catalog tests cover quarantine of new and changed entries and MCP Streamable HTTP/SSE interoperability.
A second catalog refresh omits a previously discovered tool, but the test does not inspect or require the missing tool to be disabled or removed, leaving stale-capability lifecycle behavior untested.
No final test-quality or implementation verdict is valid until lines 1001-6996 and linked route/schema/history evidence are reviewed.

Route integration verifies tools:admin for arbitrary admin-defined stdio templates, active-template enforcement, direct private-endpoint rejection in authenticated public deployment, and same-company profile target validation.

The stdio tests prove commands cannot be supplied directly on a connection, but intentionally permit arbitrary command, args, and env keys once an administrator creates a template; runtime sandbox and command provenance remain outside this evidence.
Remote endpoint defense is tested only against a direct link-local metadata URL; redirect targets, DNS rebinding, timeouts, and oversized responses are not covered in this range.

Board-initiated test calls preserve the real user actor and separately attribute the selected agent with source=test metadata, a useful responsibility distinction that the older smoke fixture does not consistently preserve.

Ask-first tests exercise pending request creation, signed arguments, approval execution, repeated side-effecting requests, rejection without execution, block policy, quarantined tools, and unassignable agents.
The rejection test explicitly accepts an invocation that remains status=awaiting_approval while approvalState=rejected, leaving a non-terminal execution status after a terminal human decision.
Profile CRUD and effective-access tests cover normal outcomes and narrowest-scope precedence but do not inject database failures or concurrency into the non-transactional create/update/delete paths.
List and projection scale, cross-profile deny semantics, and uninstall-to-revoke behavior remain untested in this range.

Tests confirm agent-scoped profiles completely replace broader company profiles in effective previews, profile copies may include assignments, and database cascades remove entries and bindings on successful profile deletion.
Delete-with-reassignment failure atomicity and duplicate-profile partial failure are not exercised; successful cascade evidence does not close those implementation risks.
Profile routes enforce board-only mutation, viewer-safe read access, cross-company read hiding, and mutation denial.

The safe example installation is tested as idempotent and verifies allow, deny, and audit decisions, but no real company agent exists in the fixture, so it misses the implementation path that attributes smoke audit records to the first production agent.
MCP JSON preview proves raw header values are not echoed and link connection setup stores them as secrets, while payload-size and object-count limits remain untested.
Class-3 static lease tests verify exact allowlist admission and fail-closed rejection without connection or binding residue.
Google Sheets tests intentionally assert that a cross-company conflict returns the exact spreadsheet id, codifying a cross-tenant resource-identifier disclosure instead of a non-enumerating error.

Agent-initiated user OAuth verifies active-run responsibleUserId snapshot matching, separate user/workspace secret sets, and consent-card resolution, but does not prove current membership, a versioned responsibility contract, or requested-scope restriction.
No final test-quality or reuse judgment is valid until the remaining OAuth, lifecycle, concurrency, runtime, and route cases are read.

OAuth route tests strongly bind callbacks to the initiating user and exact session, reject anonymous, other-user, other-session, and permission-downgraded callbacks, and retain state after unauthorized attempts.
End-to-end OAuth tests verify PKCE, secret-backed token storage, absence of raw tokens in connection config, app activation, catalog grouping, and browser redirect behavior.

DCR tests validate exact registered metadata, strict response rejection, HTTPS-or-loopback constraints, and reuse, but concurrency is exercised only through two calls on one service instance, so the process-local single-flight masks multi-instance duplicate registration.
Refresh tests across two service instances prove one database-leased upstream refresh and reuse of the new access token under the ordinary success path.

Refresh tests do not simulate the critical window where secret rotation succeeds and the guarded connection CAS subsequently loses, so latest-version credential mutation outside the lease remains untested.
invalid_grant, superseded refresh-version, abandoned lease, client-credentials, and missing-refresh-token paths have useful fail-closed coverage.
No callback test in this range injects failure after state deletion but before token, secret, grant, health, or catalog completion, leaving one-shot retry semantics unverified.
Attention-feed tests verify health, quarantine, pending approval, and profile-new-tool projections, but do not test the implementation's full-invocation and full-catalog query growth.
Listing pending approvals cancels missing or invalid signatures and preserves valid ones, but the test does not require an audit event or reason record for this security-relevant state mutation.
New-tool review tests cover exact all-item decisions and mixed allow/keep-blocked results, but not concurrent catalog arrival, watermark races, transaction failure, or partial writes.

Connect rollback tests verify application, connection, and catalog cleanup on health failure and restoration of a revived app/connection, but omit credential secrets, bindings, grants, and runtime-slot residue under failure.
OAuth metadata redirect testing confirms manual redirect handling prevents a protected-resource redirect to link-local metadata, a strong reusable SSRF regression test.
Generic pasted-link OAuth verifies discovery, PKCE/token exchange, secret-backed storage, and credential scope metadata; scope escalation and response-size/time limits remain untested.
Smoke Lab URLs are rejected from the production OAuth pipeline unless the connection is explicitly marked as the fixture, reducing accidental demo/production credential mixing.
The remaining gallery-finish, lifecycle, audit, runtime, CRUD-race, and cleanup tests must be read before final judgment.

Gallery-finish tests cover idempotent profile/policy replacement, complete review of quarantined actions, Notion-specific mutation classification, cross-company denial, and a real injected late-write failure that proves transaction rollback restores entries, bindings, and policies.
Reconnect testing proves successful in-place secret rotation without duplicate references but does not test failed health validation, database failure, or recovery of the prior working secret.
Runtime slot tests cover stop/restart behavior, activity attribution, board routes, tools:manage_runtime permission, and rejection of unsupported remote runtime controls.
Viewer regression tests broadly protect application, connection, health, catalog, profile, policy, trust-rule, example, and runtime mutation routes while retaining read access where intended.

Application deletion tests cover friendly linked-connection conflicts, last-connection application archive, multiple-connection preservation, normalized UID uniqueness, and a database-level delete/create race guarded by NO ACTION foreign-key behavior.
Archive tests do not assert revocation or suspension of grants, profile bindings, catalog entries, or local runtime slots, leaving authority and execution cleanup unverified.
Run-decision tests exercise one invocation with one action request only and do not expose the implementation's single-value map behavior for multiple requests.
Connection activity tests verify issue and resolver enrichment plus lifecycle event ordering and display-name projection.
Runtime health tests cover stale slots, capacity/restart signals, degraded active connections, durable audit-write counters, draft/disabled exclusions, and hosted local-stdio restrictions.
Health-sweep testing uses one connection and does not cover the implementation's cross-company full-table load, database limit omission, starvation, or multi-worker claim behavior.
Secret-resolution failure tests confirm fail-closed health state and value-free audit records.
Install synchronization tests cover only adding one agent install and the resulting access extension; they never remove an install, so the stale profile-binding revocation defect is not caught.

Risk-classification tests cover namespace and camelCase verbs plus annotations and Notion's explicit catalog, but explicitly expect non-Notion move_pages to be read, codifying fail-open handling for an unrecognized mutation verb.

No test covers broker response scope escalation, actual expiresAt enforcement, concurrent default rate-limit reservations, post-mint audit failure, duplicate grant selection, profile list scale, or callback state loss after downstream failure.
The complete 6996-line test source is now covered; final unit status still requires history, route authority, database schemas and migrations, and execution of the focused tests.
